title: HDR highlight viewer
blurb: Renders a 1x-8x SDR white sun and ramp into side-by-side 'standard' and 'extended' float16 canvases and samples stored pixels to confirm tone mapping applies only at display time.
question: Does creating a float16 2D canvas with toneMapping: { mode: 'extended' } vs 'standard' alter the underlying pixel values read back through getImageData?
result: Sampling the sun centre via getImageData({ pixelFormat: 'rgba-float16' }) returns identical 5.000 channel values on both canvases in Chrome 153, confirming stored pixels are unaltered. Visible HDR luminance separation is a manual observation requiring an HDR display and Chrome 160+.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 158.0.8127.36 (Linux, headless, SDR) with --enable-experimental-web-platform-features on 2026-11-28; earlier Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12

friction.summary: Visible HDR highlight separation cannot be verified programmatically on headless SDR displays and script cannot query exact display headroom
friction.repro: Open the viewer on an SDR display or headless browser where matchMedia('(dynamic-range: high)').matches is false; both canvases render identically even when extended mode is active.
friction.workaround: Validate stored HDR pixel retention via getImageData({ pixelFormat: 'rgba-float16' }) and pair with matchMedia('(dynamic-range: high)') for manual HDR display checks.
